````text
1	Outline is a fast, collaborative knowledge base built for teams. It's built with React and TypeScript in both frontend and backend, uses a real-time collaboration engine, and is designed for excellent performance and user experience. The backend is a Koa server with an RPC API and uses PostgreSQL and Redis. The application can be self-hosted or used as a cloud service.
2	
3	There is a web client which is fully responsive and works on mobile devices.
4	
5	**Monorepo Structure:**
6	
7	- **`app/`** - React web application with MobX state management
8	- **`server/`** - Koa API server with Sequelize ORM and background workers
9	- **`shared/`** - Shared TypeScript types, utilities, and editor components
10	- **`plugins/`** - Plugin system for extending functionality
11	- **`public/`** - Static assets served directly
12	- **Various config files** - TypeScript, Vite, Vitest, oxfmt, Oxlint configurations
13	
14	Refer to /docs/ARCHITECTURE.md for detailed architecture documentation.
15	
16	## Instructions
17	
18	You're an expert in the following areas:
19	
20	- TypeScript
21	- React and React Router
22	- MobX and MobX-React
23	- Node.js and Koa
24	- Sequelize ORM
25	- PostgreSQL
26	- Redis
27	- HTML, CSS and Styled Components
28	- Prosemirror (rich text editor)
29	- WebSockets and real-time collaboration
30	
31	## General Guidelines
32	
33	- Critical – Do not create new markdown (.md) files.
34	- Use early returns for readability.
35	- Emphasize type safety and static analysis.
36	- Follow consistent oxfmt formatting.
37	- Do not replace smart quotes ("") or ('') with simple quotes ("").
38	- Do not add translation strings manually; they will be extracted automatically from the codebase.
39	
40	## Dependencies and Upgrading
41	
42	- Use yarn for all dependency management.
43	- After updating dependency versions, install to update lockfiles:
44	
45	```bash
46	yarn install
47	```
48	
49	- When adding a `resolutions` entry to address a security advisory in a transitive dependency, target only the specific vulnerable descriptors using the `name@npm:<range>` syntax rather than overriding the package globally. Inspect `yarn.lock` to find the exact ranges requested by upstream packages and add one entry per vulnerable range, e.g.:
50	
51	```json
52	"resolutions": {
53	  "qs@npm:^6.5.2": "^6.14.2",
54	  "qs@npm:^6.11.0": "^6.14.2",
55	  "qs@npm:^6.14.0": "^6.14.2"
56	}
57	```
58	
59	This keeps overrides scoped to the affected dependents and avoids forcing unrelated consumers onto an incompatible version.
60	
61	## TypeScript Usage
62	
63	- Use strict mode.
64	- Avoid "unknown" unless absolutely necessary.
65	- Never use "any".
66	- Prefer type definitions; avoid type assertions (as, !).
67	- Always use curly braces for if statements.
68	- Avoid # for private properties.
69	- Prefer interface over type for object shapes.
70	
71	## Classes & Code Organization
72	
73	### Class Member Order
74	
75	1. Public static variables
76	2. Public static methods
77	3. Public variables
78	4. Public methods
79	5. Protected variables & methods
80	6. Private variables & methods
81	
82	### Exports
83	
84	- Exported members must appear at the top of the file.
85	- Always use named exports for new components & classes.
86	- Document ALL public/exported functions with JSDoc.
87	
88	## React Usage
89	
90	- Use functional components with hooks.
91	- Event handlers should be prefixed with "handle", like "handleClick" for onClick.
92	- Avoid unnecessary re-renders by using React.memo, useMemo, and useCallback appropriately.
93	- Use descriptive prop types with TypeScript interfaces.
94	- Do not import React unless it is used directly.
95	- Use styled-components for component styling.
96	- Ensure high accessibility (a11y) standards using ARIA roles and semantic HTML.
97	
98	## MobX State Management
99	
100	- Use MobX stores for global state management.
101	- Keep stores in `app/stores/`.
102	- Use `observable`, `action`, and `computed` decorators appropriately.
103	- Prefer computed values over manual calculations in render.
104	- Keep business logic in stores, not components.
105	
106	## Database & ORM
107	
108	- Use Sequelize models in `server/models/`.
109	- Generate migrations with Sequelize CLI:
110	
111	```bash
112	yarn sequelize migration:create --name=add-field-to-table
113	```
114	
115	- Run migrations with `yarn db:migrate`.
116	- Use transactions for multi-table operations.
117	- Add appropriate indexes for query performance.
118	- Always handle database errors gracefully.
119	
120	## API Design
121	
122	- RESTful endpoints under `/api/`.
123	- Authentication endpoints under `/auth/`.
124	- Use consistent error responses.
125	- Validate request data using the validation middleware and schemas
126	- Use presenters to format API responses.
127	- Keep API routes thin, use model methods for business logic, or commands if logic spans multiple models.
128	
129	## Authentication & Authorization
130	
131	- JWT tokens for authentication.
132	- Policies in `server/policies/` for authorization.
133	- Use cancan-style ability checks.
134	- Use authenticated middleware for protected routes.
135	- Always verify user permissions before data access.
136	
137	## Real-time Collaboration
138	
139	- WebSocket connections for real-time updates.
140	- Use Y.js for collaborative editing.
141	- Handle connection state changes gracefully.
142	
143	## Documentation
144	
145	- All public/exported functions & classes must have JSDoc.
146	- Include:
147	  - Description
148	  - @param and @return (start lowercase, end with period)
149	  - @throws if applicable
150	- Add a newline between the description and the @ block.
151	- Use correct punctuation.
152	
153	## Testing
154	
155	- Run tests with Vitest:
156	
157	```bash
158	# Run a specific test file (preferred)
159	yarn test path/to/test.spec.ts
160	
161	# Run every test (avoid)
162	yarn test
163	
164	# Run test suites (avoid)
165	yarn test:app      # All frontend tests
166	yarn test:server   # All backend tests
167	yarn test:shared   # All shared code tests
168	```
169	
170	- Write unit tests for utilities and business logic in a collocated .test.ts file.
171	- Do not create new test directories
172	- Mock external dependencies appropriately in **mocks** folder.
173	- Aim for high code coverage but focus on critical paths.
174	
175	## Code Quality
176	
177	- Use Oxlint for linting: `yarn lint`
178	- Format code with oxfmt: `yarn format`
179	- Check types with TypeScript: `yarn tsc`
180	- Pre-commit hooks run automatically via Husky.
181	- Fix linting issues before committing.
182	
183	## Error Handling
184	
185	- Use custom error classes in `server/errors.ts`.
186	- Always catch and handle errors appropriately.
187	- Log errors with appropriate context.
188	- Return user-friendly error messages.
189	- Never expose sensitive information in errors.
190	
191	## Performance
192	
193	- Use React.memo for expensive components.
194	- Implement pagination for large lists.
195	- Use database indexes effectively.
196	- Cache expensive computations.
197	- Monitor performance with appropriate tools.
198	- Lazy load routes and components where appropriate.
199	
200	## Security
201	
202	- Sanitize all user input.
203	- Always use `sanitizeUrl()` when setting `href` or `src` from user-controlled data in ProseMirror `toDOM` methods, regardless of whether it is imported via an alias or a relative path. Unlike React components, `toDOM` writes raw DOM and does not sanitize attribute values.
204	- Use CSRF protection.

67	  const sidebarContext = useSidebarContext();

75	    }
76	  }, [expansion, expanded, hasChildDocuments, node.id]);
77	
78	  React.useEffect(() => {
79	    if (
80	      isActiveDocument &&
81	      (hasChildDocuments || sidebarContext !== "collections")
82	    ) {

84	    }
85	  }, [
86	    fetchChildDocuments,
87	    node.id,
88	    hasChildDocuments,
89	    sidebarContext,
90	    isActiveDocument,
91	  ]);
92	
93	  const insertDraftChild = !!(
94	    activeDocument?.isDraft &&
95	    activeDocument?.isActive &&
96	    activeDocument?.parentDocumentId === node.id

99	  const draftNavNode = insertDraftChild

120	  const observerOptions = React.useMemo(
121	    () => ({ root: scrollRoot, rootMargin: ROOT_MARGIN }),

149	      });
150	    }
151	  }, [isActiveDocument, sidebarContext]);

153	  return (
154	    <>
155	      <div ref={placeholderRef} style={{ minHeight: ROW_HEIGHT }}>

157	          <DocumentLinkInner {...props} hasChildren={nodeChildren.length > 0} />
158	        ) : null}
159	      </div>
160	      <Folder expanded={expanded}>
161	        {nodeChildren.map((childNode, childIndex) => (
162	          <DocumentLink
163	            key={childNode.id}
164	            collection={collection}
165	            membership={props.membership}
166	            node={childNode}
167	            activeDocument={activeDocument}
168	            prefetchDocument={props.prefetchDocument}
169	            isDraft={childNode.isDraft}
170	            depth={props.depth + 1}
171	            index={childIndex}

173	          />
174	        ))}

182	};

    );

Research confirms this is mostly a wiring gap, not new infrastructure — good news for scope. Here's the picture:

**Already built and just sitting unused:**
- Backend already tracks per-user "have I viewed this doc" via the `View` model, and `Document.lastViewedAt` is exposed to the frontend.
- The frontend already has an `isBadgedNew` getter (`!lastViewedAt && created <14 days ago`) used for a "New" text badge on `DocumentListItem` (the recently-updated list).
- There's already a **sidebar dot primitive** (`UnreadBadge` component + `unreadBadge` prop threaded through `SidebarLink`/`DocumentRow`), currently only wired up in `SharedWithMeLink.tsx` for unread *notifications* — not for "never opened."

**The actual gap:** `DocumentLink.tsx` (the component that renders each doc row in the collection sidebar tree) never passes `unreadBadge` at all. Wiring it up the same way `SharedWithMeLink.tsx` does is most of the work.

**One real wrinkle:** `documents.list` (used to hydrate the sidebar tree) doesn't apply the `withViews` scope, so `lastViewedAt` may come back `undefined` for docs the sidebar has loaded but that were never fetched via `documents.info`/`documents.viewed`/etc. — meaning the dot could be wrong (always "unread") until that's fixed or worked around.

_**Agent (claude-sonnet-5 2026-09-16 15:36:07Z)**_

Direct code inspection turned up something important: **the `withViews` gap the earlier research flagged doesn't actually exist.** `documents.list` (and `fetchChildDocuments`, which is what populates the sidebar tree's `Document` objects) both go through `Document.withMembershipScope()`, and that method has included the `withViews` scope since PR #9134 (May 2025) — confirmed via `git log -p` on that method. So `lastViewedAt` is already reliably populated wherever the sidebar loads document data. I'm not going to introduce a fake fix for a problem that isn't there.

Now wiring the actual sidebar dot using the existing `isBadgedNew` getter (same "never viewed" signal already used for the collection's "New" badge), in `DocumentLink.tsx`:

_**Agent (claude-sonnet-5 2026-09-16 15:39:11Z)**_

Here's what changed and why:

**File: `app/components/Sidebar/components/DocumentLink.tsx`** (only file touched)

```diff
+  const unreadBadge =
+    !!document?.isBadgedNew && document.createdBy?.id !== user.id;
...
       icon={iconElement}
+      unreadBadge={unreadBadge}
       canEdit={canUpdate}
```

This computes the same "unread" signal Outline already uses for the yellow "New" badge on `DocumentListItem` (`document.isBadgedNew`: never viewed by this user), excludes documents the current user created themselves (same exclusion `DocumentListItem` applies), and passes it into `DocumentRow`'s existing `unreadBadge` prop — which already renders the small accent-colored dot via `SidebarLink`/`UnreadBadge`. That prop and dot component already existed and were just never connected to the collection sidebar tree (only `SharedWithMeLink.tsx` used them, for a different signal — unread notifications).

No backend changes were needed: I verified `documents.list` and `fetchChildDocuments` (the two paths that populate `Document` objects for the sidebar tree) already go through `Document.withMembershipScope()`, which has included the `withViews` scope since May 2025 (PR #9134) — so `lastViewedAt`/`isBadgedNew` is already reliable there. The earlier research report was wrong about that gap; I confirmed via `git log -p` on the method rather than taking its word for it.

One caveat worth knowing: a sidebar row only gets a real `Document` object (and thus a dot) once it's been loaded into the store — for docs that haven't been fetched yet (e.g. deep unexpanded tree nodes), the row falls back to lightweight `NavigationNode` data and just won't show a dot until it loads. That's consistent with how title/icon already degrade in this component, not a regression.

Typecheck and lint are clean on this file. Want me to also run the relevant Vitest suite (or add a test), or check this manually in the browser next?
